trust_decision.summary: A caller-supplied GitLab base URL (X-GitLab-API-URL header, or an apiUrl carried in a download token / sealed session id) is admitted only when its host matches the operator's GITLAB_API_URL or GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS set; the decision is taken in resolveTrustedGitLabApiUrl against a map built once at startup and every authenticated fetch sink is supposed to use the resolved URL rather than the caller's string.

landing_point.why: The advisory is an SSRF report for an MCP client that can pick the GitLab base URL, so a reader first opens resolveTrustedGitLabApiUrl, the function that is supposed to decide which hosts are reachable.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /mcp (Streamable HTTP, stateful and OAUTH_STATELESS_MODE) via parseAuthHeaders — tool calls issued against ctx.apiUrl
process start-up config (GITLAB_API_URL, GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS) building GITLAB_ALLOWED_API_URLS_BY_HOST

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The /downloads/:type endpoint is a separate token-authenticated media proxy, not the MCP tool surface the report describes, and it already resolves X-GitLab-API-URL through index.ts:1818, so a solver can argue the download path is a neighbouring feature and already covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS exists so one deployment can route a single MCP server to several trusted GitLab instances (connection pool per host). Pinning every request to GITLAB_API_URL, or rejecting any host that is not the primary one, fixes the report but breaks documented multi-instance routing and the download proxy for secondary hosts.

O6_input_shapes: bare host or host:port without scheme (gitlab.example.com, gitlab.example.com:8443)
http:// versus https:// (both accepted, the stored configured URL is what gets fetched)

the same value arriving as X-GitLab-API-URL header (index.ts:13284, downloads/proxy.ts:122) versus an apiUrl embedded in an encrypted _token (utils/download-token.ts:42-60) versus a sealed Mcp-Session-Id u field (stateless/session-id.ts:56-68)
requested URL carrying userinfo, a fragment or a different path — discarded because the mapped configured URL is returned

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second 'resolve the caller's API URL' implementation in the download proxy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the proxy needs the same header handling for streaming, so a maintainer could plausibly have written its own resolve step instead of reusing parseAuthHeaders; it already duplicates the enableDynamicApiUrl gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: apiUrl carried in the sealed Mcp-Session-Id (u field) and trusted on later requests without re-running the allowlist (index.ts:13526)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: stateless mode serializes the whole auth context so a pod can rebuild it; a maintainer extending that payload with apiUrl need not re-check the host on replay.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ctx.apiUrl embedded into a download token and re-used by /downloads
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: buildDownloadUrl reuses the session context to make self-contained URLs, so a maintainer adding a field there could extend the reachable URL surface without touching the allowlist.

O9_family: server-side request forgery (CWE-918) via a caller-selected GitLab API base URL

O10_build.toolchain: npm install then npm run build (tsc -> build/index.js); tests run through node --test with tsx/esm (package.json:46-64)
O10_build.project_tests: test/dynamic-api-url-allowlist.test.ts (starts a real MCP server plus mock GitLab and an attacker server, asserts untrusted hosts get zero hits), test/dynamic-api-url-test.ts, test/multi-server-test.ts, test/remote-auth-simple-test.ts, test/test-remote-downloads.ts; all use local mock servers (test/utils/mock-gitlab-server.ts, test/utils/server-launcher.ts) so they run offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Stop honouring X-GitLab-API-URL (or pin getEffectiveApiUrl to GITLAB_API_URL) so the reported header can no longer reach any fetch, without keeping the allowlisted multi-host path working.
